SR-CON-001.text: **Self-contained:** the default distribution MUST run with zero external network dependencies (no SaaS, no cloud API, no phone-home, no CDN assets, no package fetch at runtime).

SR-CON-002.text: **Local-first:** all processing, storage, indexing, embedding, inference and UI serving happen inside the customer-controlled boundary by default; the system MUST function fully offline.

SR-CON-003.text: **No egress by default:** outbound traffic MUST be denied by default via network policy and application-level egress gateway; any permitted egress is allowlisted, logged and attributable.

SR-CON-004.text: **Everything configurable, safely:** every behavior in this document that says "configurable" MUST be a typed, versioned, validated, auditable setting with a safe default (§12.3).

SR-CON-005.text: **LLM-optional:** ingestion, graph construction, validation, deterministic query, impact analysis, lineage and reporting MUST work with no LLM present.

SR-CON-006.text: **Evidence-first:** every returned fact carries source, method (asserted/derived/inferred/curated), confidence, freshness and policy-filter notice.

SR-CON-007.text: **Clean-room and license-clean:** study external products and papers for ideas only; produce an independent implementation, SBOM and license report per release.

SR-CON-008.text: **Adapters over lock-in:** no component outside an adapter may import a vendor-specific graph, vector, model, bus or storage SDK. Enforced by architecture tests.

SR-CON-009.text: **Vendor-neutral data ownership:** customers can export all data, ontology, config and audit trails in open formats at any time (§7.9).

SR-CON-010.text: Cloud capabilities MUST be delivered as **Service Provider plugins** (e.g., object storage, managed graph DB, managed search, KMS/HSM, IdP, queue, LLM endpoint, monitoring sink) selectable per capability, per tenant.

SR-CON-011.text: Every plugin MUST ship a **Data-Flow Manifest** declaring data classes sent/received, destinations, regions, retention and whether data can leave the tenant boundary. Installation MUST display it and require admin approval; the egress gateway enforces it at runtime.

SR-CON-012.text: Provide reference adapters for the three hyperscalers' object storage, KMS, identity federation and managed graph/search where available (e.g., Amazon Neptune/OpenSearch/S3/KMS, Azure Blob/Key Vault/Entra ID/Cosmos Gremlin, GCP GCS/KMS/Cloud Identity).

SR-CON-013.text: Provide infrastructure-as-code modules (Terraform/OpenTofu, Helm) for DP-3/DP-4 with security-hardened defaults, private networking, and no public endpoints by default.

SR-CON-014.text: A tenant MUST be able to switch a capability between local and cloud providers via migration tooling (e.g., local object store → cloud bucket) with verification and rollback.

SR-ARC-001.text: **Modular monolith first, service-extractable:** modules communicate through typed interfaces/events and MUST be separable into independently scalable services without code rewrite (preserves the prior `NFR-MAINT-001` boundary).

SR-ARC-002.text: **Ports-and-adapters:** Graph Store, Vector Store, Search, Object Store, Relational Store, Event Bus, Model Provider, Identity Provider, Secret/KMS, Scheduler and Notification are ports with versioned contracts and a conformance test kit.

SR-ARC-003.text: **Event backbone:** an append-only event log (pluggable: embedded log for DP-0; NATS JetStream/Kafka-class for clustered) carries ingestion, mutation, policy and audit events; consumers are idempotent (outbox pattern).

SR-ARC-004.text: **Single canonical contract per concept:** one versioned schema registry for entities, edges, events, QueryPlan, agent contract, config and plugin manifest; all APIs and UIs derive from it (generated, not hand-copied).

SR-ARC-005.text: **Distributed by design:** stateless API/query/worker tiers scale horizontally; stateful tiers (graph, vector, search, relational, object, log) support replication and partitioning per backend capability.

SR-ARC-006.text: **Consistency model documented and tested:** strong consistency within a graph partition for writes and read-your-writes for the writer; eventual consistency for derived indexes (vector, search, materialized views) with measurable lag SLOs and a staleness indicator surfaced to users.

SR-ARC-007.text: **Exactly-once effects** via idempotency keys, deterministic IDs and replay-safe mutations; at-least-once delivery acceptable at transport level.

SR-ARC-008.text: **Hybrid logical clocks / bitemporal fields** on all mutations (valid time, transaction time) so federated and replayed data order deterministically.

SR-ARC-009.text: **Federation:** queries MAY span multiple graph backends and multiple sites (hub-and-spoke or mesh) with partial-result semantics, per-site policy enforcement and no raw-data movement unless permitted.

SR-ARC-010.text: **Sandboxed extension runtime:** plugins execute in isolated containers or WASM sandboxes with declared capabilities, CPU/memory/egress limits and signed manifests (§12.5).

SR-ARC-011.text: **Architecture fitness tests** in CI: forbidden imports, layering rules, adapter-only vendor SDK usage, no hand-maintained inventories, no cross-tenant code paths without tenant context.

SR-ARC-012.text: **Mandatory ADR process:** every decision that changes a port, a default component or a supported-backend tier needs an ADR with alternatives, license review and benchmark evidence.

SR-GDB-001.text: All graph access MUST go through the **Graph Store Port** exposing: schema ops, bulk load, transactional upsert (idempotent by canonical ID), traversal, path, neighborhood, aggregation, full-scan with cursor, index management, snapshot/export, health and statistics.

SR-GDB-002.text: Each adapter MUST publish a **Capability Manifest** (example in §5.6). The planner uses it to choose pushdown vs in-engine execution and to refuse or degrade unsupported plans *explicitly* (never silently).

SR-GDB-003.text: A **backend-neutral conformance suite** (contract tests + golden queries + performance probes + failure injection) MUST gate every adapter. Backend-specific behavior (e.g., HugeGraph 1.7 not honoring UNIQUE edge indexes, requiring SECONDARY + sort-key emulation) is recorded in the manifest, not scattered in code.

SR-GDB-004.text: **Certification tiers:** Tier A *Certified* (full conformance, benchmarked, HA validated, supported under SLA); Tier B *Compatible* (documented capability gaps); Tier C *Community/Experimental*. Marketing MUST NOT claim support beyond the tier.

SR-GDB-005.text: **Polyglot persistence:** each logical graph domain (e.g., org, code, incident, lineage, meta) MAY bind to a different backend and tier (hot/warm/cold); cross-domain **bridge edges** are resolved by the federation layer.

SR-GDB-006.text: **Online migration** between backends (export → verify counts/checksums/golden queries → dual-write or cutover → rollback) MUST be supported for Tier A pairs.

SR-GDB-007.text: **Virtual/zero-ETL graph mode:** optionally expose existing relational/lakehouse data as a graph view through declarative mappings (OBDA/virtual-graph style) without copying data.

SR-GDB-008.text: **Multi-model graph support:** property graph (LPG) and RDF are both first-class; RDF-star/reification patterns and LPG↔RDF round-trip mappings MUST be defined and tested.

SR-GDB-009.text: **Graph versioning:** every mutation produces an `EntityRevision`; point-in-time ("as-of") reads and diffs between revisions MUST be supported (full snapshot/diff at P1).

SR-GDB-010.text: **Embedded engine option** for DP-0/edge nodes with no server process, and an in-memory engine for tests only (selection is explicit configuration, never a silent fallback).

SR-GDB-011.text: **Relational metadata/config store:** PostgreSQL as the clustered default, SQLite for single-node DP-0; ports allow customer-standard engines (SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL/MariaDB) at P2.

SR-GDB-012.text: **Object/raw store:** filesystem (DP-0), S3-compatible (clustered), and cloud blob adapters. Raw captures are immutable, content-addressed (SHA-256), encrypted, and retention-managed.

SR-GDB-013.text: **Event bus adapters:** embedded log, NATS JetStream-class, Kafka/Redpanda-class, RabbitMQ, cloud queues.

SR-GDB-014.text: **Cache:** in-process plus a Redis-protocol-compatible adapter; every cache key MUST include tenant, policy-version and graph-revision.

SR-GDB-015.text: **Durable workflow engine** built in (retry, timers, human-approval steps, sagas); optional adapters for Temporal/Airflow/Dagster/Prefect-class orchestrators.

SR-GDB-016.text: **Component license matrix:** every bundled and optional component is classified (permissive / weak copyleft / strong copyleft or network-copyleft / source-available / commercial). Anything other than permissive MUST NOT be bundled without legal sign-off and MUST be offered as bring-your-own where needed.

SR-VDB-001.text: **Vector Store Port:** upsert/delete by ID with metadata, filtered kNN, hybrid (dense + sparse/BM25), namespace-per-tenant, snapshot/restore, index rebuild, embedding-model version tracking.

SR-VDB-002.text: **Adapters:** embedded (FAISS/hnswlib/USearch/LanceDB-class), PostgreSQL pgvector, Qdrant, Milvus, Weaviate, Chroma, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch k-NN, Redis-compatible vector, Vespa, graph-native vector indexes (e.g., Neo4j), plus cloud-managed (Pinecone, Azure AI Search, Vertex AI Vector Search, Atlas Vector Search) under DP-3/4 only.

SR-VDB-003.text: **Index strategies configurable:** HNSW, IVF-PQ, DiskANN-class disk indexes, scalar/product/binary quantization, filtered-search strategies, per-collection recall/latency targets.

SR-VDB-004.text: **Multi-vector and multimodal:** text, code, table, image, audio-transcript, and node/graph embeddings; late-interaction (ColBERT-style) and sparse-learned (SPLADE-style) as optional retrievers.

SR-VDB-005.text: **Embedding governance:** embeddings are derived data; they inherit the classification and access policy of their source, are deleted when the source is erased (§14.3), and are re-generated on model change with versioned side-by-side indexes and cut-over.

SR-VDB-006.text: **Full-text/search port:** BM25 keyword, phrase, fuzzy, facets, highlighting, multilingual analyzers; adapters for embedded engine (Tantivy/SQLite-FTS class), PostgreSQL FTS, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch class.

SR-VDB-007.text: A deployment with **no vector store** MUST still pass the core NL acceptance suite using graph + full-text retrieval (degraded semantic recall is acceptable and MUST be signalled).

SR-QRY-001.text: The compiler MUST accept EOQL, Gremlin, openCypher, GQL (subset first), SPARQL, SQL (analytics) and NL-produced plans, validate them against the ontology and the caller's policy, and lower them per the Capability Manifest.

SR-QRY-002.text: **Never execute raw model- or user-generated graph queries** without schema-aware validation, policy rewrite, depth/timeout/expansion/cost limits and expensive-pattern detection. Raw dialect access is an admin-gated, audited feature.

SR-QRY-003.text: **Query Explain:** every query returns (on request) the plan, chosen backend(s), pushdowns, estimated vs actual cost, and the generated dialect text.

SR-QRY-004.text: **Dialect round-trip tests:** a golden corpus (≥ 500 queries per Tier A backend, growing) MUST prove IR → dialect semantic equivalence by result comparison on shared fixtures.

SR-QRY-005.text: **Parameterization everywhere;** string-built queries are forbidden (injection defense).

SR-QRY-006.text: **Saved queries, query libraries, templates and versioned "question catalog"** per tenant/workspace, shareable and permission-aware.

SR-QRY-007.text: **Result envelope:** rows/graph/table/report + evidence IDs + method flags + freshness (as-of, lag) + coverage notes + policy filters applied.

SR-QRY-008.text: **Graph algorithm library** callable from plans (≥ 60 algorithms by P1): shortest/k-shortest/all-simple paths, reachability, SCC/WCC, topological order and cycle detection, dominators/critical path, PageRank/personalized PageRank, betweenness/closeness/degree/eigenvector centrality, community detection (Leiden/Louvain/label propagation), triangle/clustering/k-core, similarity (Jaccard/cosine/Adamic-Adar), node embeddings (node2vec/GraphSAGE-class), link prediction, motif matching, temporal paths, flow/cut, subgraph isomorphism/pattern matching. Each declares complexity and sampling/approximation modes.

SR-QRY-009.text: **Incremental / precomputed accelerators:** transitive-closure or reachability indexes for impact queries, materialized views per persona, summary edges, and top-k caches, all invalidated by graph-revision events.

SR-QRY-010.text: **Federated query** across backends and sites with per-source policy enforcement and partial results.

SR-QRY-011.text: **Time travel:** `AS OF`, `BETWEEN`, `DIFF` over revisions for every query class where backends or the revision store allow.

SR-QRY-012.text: **Multilingual query front-ends** (NL, EOQL) with locale-aware date/number handling.

SR-ING-001.text: **Connector SDK** (Python and TypeScript at P0; Go/Java at P1) with a stable contract: `discover`, `authenticate`, `fetch(cursor)`, `schema`, `health`, `metrics`, `capabilities`, `deletion_semantics`; connectors run sandboxed with declared scopes.

SR-ING-002.text: Resiliency: pagination, rate-limit adaptation, retry with jitter, circuit breaker, checkpoint/cursor, partial-failure isolation, DLQ, replay, dry-run, backfill and incremental sync.

SR-ING-003.text: **Change capture:** polling, webhooks, CDC (log-based where the source supports it), file watchers, stream consumers; deletes handled by tombstones with configurable semantics (soft delete, retire edge, hard delete on policy).

SR-ING-004.text: **Credential isolation:** connector secrets live only in the secret store, scoped per tenant/connector, rotated, never logged, never visible to plugins other than the owning connector.

SR-ING-005.text: **Connector marketplace-ready packaging:** signed manifest, version, compatibility range, data-flow manifest, test fixtures, health contract.

SR-ING-006.text: **Streaming and batch share one pipeline:** the same stages and mapping specs serve both; back-pressure and priority lanes per tenant.

SR-ING-007.text: **Large-JSON handling:** streaming parse (never load whole file), gz/zstd/archive support, malformed-record quarantine with line/offset pointers, numeric precision and Unicode/timezone normalization, binary blob offload.

SR-ING-010.text: The **Schema Profiler** MUST infer types, nullability, cardinality, uniqueness, enumerations, formats (email, UUID, URL, IP/CIDR, ISO date/time, currency, phone, IBAN, ARN/URN, git SHA, ticket keys like `ABC-123`, file paths), nesting shape, and drift across versions of a payload.

SR-ING-011.text: **Entity detection:** record types from top-level arrays/envelopes/discriminator fields; nested objects classified as *embedded value*, *child entity*, or *reference* using a scored heuristic (key presence, size, reuse across parents, naming, user override).

SR-ING-012.text: **Key detection:** natural/surrogate key candidates; composite keys; stability scoring across runs; canonical ID minting strategy per type (deterministic, namespaced, collision-safe).

SR-ING-013.text: **Relationship discovery — explicit:** foreign-key-like fields, `$ref`/JSON Pointer, URLs to known entities, `*_id`/`parent`/`owner` conventions, join-table detection (junction → edge with properties), polymorphic `type`+`id` pairs, array-of-IDs, hierarchy via parent pointers or path strings.

SR-ING-014.text: **Relationship discovery — statistical:** inclusion-dependency and value-overlap discovery across datasets (MinHash/LSH containment for scale), name and embedding-based schema matching, co-occurrence, temporal proximity, co-change coupling, mention extraction in text (entity linking).

SR-ING-015.text: **Relationship discovery — operational:** service-call edges from traces/logs, config references (env var → secret → account), IaC dependency edges, build/runtime dependencies from SBOM and lockfiles, code call/import graphs (tree-sitter and SCIP/LSIF-class indexers), SQL lineage parsing, access-log derived usage edges.

SR-ING-016.text: **Edge classes and honesty:** every edge is `ASSERTED` (source says so), `DERIVED` (deterministic rule), `INFERRED` (statistical/ML/LLM), or `CURATED` (human-approved), with confidence and method. Inferred edges are excluded from "authoritative" answers unless the query opts in. *(Analogous to Graphify's EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS confidence tags, extended with CURATED and DERIVED.)*

SR-ING-017.text: **Ontology induction:** propose classes, properties, relation types and hierarchies from data; present for steward approval in the Mapping Studio; support *ontology-first*, *data-first* and *hybrid* modes.

SR-ING-018.text: **Link prediction / graph completion** (heuristic and learned, e.g., translational and GNN-class models) proposes missing edges into a review queue; auto-assertion only above a tenant-configured threshold.

SR-ING-019.text: **Mapping DSL:** declarative, versioned, diff-able mappings (YAML/JSON) with RML/R2RML and JSON-LD `@context` import/export; generated by inference, editable by humans, testable on samples.

SR-ING-020.text: **Schema drift handling:** new/changed/removed fields trigger drift events, auto-compatible mapping updates when safe, and steward review when not; mappings are pinned per run for reproducibility.

SR-ING-030.text: Deterministic rules first (exact keys, normalized emails/IDs), then probabilistic (blocking via sorted-neighborhood/canopy/LSH; pairwise similarity with string/phonetic/numeric/date/embedding features; Fellegi–Sunter-class scoring and/or trained classifiers).

SR-ING-031.text: **Collective resolution** using graph context (shared neighbors, co-authorship, same repo/team) and transitive clustering with constraints; **survivorship rules** produce golden records with per-attribute source precedence.

SR-ING-032.text: Every merge is **explainable, reversible (unmerge), audited**; three bands (auto-merge / human review / reject) with tenant-set thresholds and an active-learning review queue.

SR-ING-033.text: **Cross-source ID crosswalk** persisted as first-class graph structure (`SAME_AS` with confidence and evidence) so aliases resolve at query time.

SR-ING-040.text: Derived graphs are computed **incrementally** from mutation events; full rebuild MUST be possible and verified equivalent to the incremental result.

SR-ING-041.text: **Graphify-class artifacts:** auto-generate portable `graph.json`, interactive HTML, and a markdown/wiki report per graph or subgraph; support export to Obsidian/Markdown vaults; support post-commit/post-merge hooks and PR-impact triage (rank open change requests by graph impact; flag overlapping-community conflicts).

SR-ING-042.text: **Traversal-first retrieval** (no embeddings required) is the baseline retrieval mode; embeddings enhance recall but are never prerequisite (consistent with SR-CON-005).

SR-ING-043.text: **Pre-aggregation:** per-type degree/centrality, per-edge-class reachability, and domain-to-domain bridge statistics are maintained to answer overview and impact questions within latency targets.

SR-ING-050.text: Validation rules with severities (`INFO/WARN/ERROR/BLOCKER`), remediation suggestions, quarantine with replay, and a data-quality scorecard (completeness, freshness, uniqueness, consistency, confidence distribution) per source and per domain.

SR-ING-051.text: **Freshness SLOs** per connector with alerting and a user-visible "knowledge age" on every answer.

SR-ING-052.text: **Idempotency tests:** re-running an ingestion produces zero net graph change; interrupted runs resume without duplicates (restart-safe).

SR-ING-053.text: **Reconciliation reports** (source counts vs graph counts, orphan edges, dangling references) on schedule.

SR-ING-060.text: **Hostile-input posture:** parsers sandboxed; zip-bomb/path-traversal/XXE/deserialization defenses; file-type verification; size/time limits.

SR-ING-061.text: **Indirect prompt injection defense:** ingested text is data, never instructions; extracted passages are fenced, scanned and flagged before any LLM sees them.

SR-ING-070.text: Export formats: JSON/NDJSON, CSV, Parquet, GraphML, GEXF, GraphSON, openCypher bulk CSV, RDF (Turtle, N-Quads, JSON-LD, RDF-star), DOT/Mermaid, Markdown vault, interactive HTML; full-tenant export bundle (data + ontology + mappings + config + audit).

SR-ING-071.text: BI/analytics access: read-only JDBC/ODBC SQL views, OData, GraphQL, Arrow Flight-class bulk endpoint, notebook (Jupyter) client libraries.

SR-ONT-001.text: **Ontology service** stores ontologies as versioned artifacts (semantic versioning, diff, migration plans, deprecation lifecycle). Every graph element pins `ontology_version`.

SR-ONT-002.text: **Import/export:** OWL 2 (RDF/XML, Turtle, Manchester), RDFS, SKOS, JSON Schema, JSON-LD contexts, LinkML-style schemas, Protégé project interop, CSV glossaries; export of the active ontology to OWL and SHACL shapes.

SR-ONT-003.text: **Ontology Studio** (UI): visual class/property editor, relationship canvas, constraint editor, glossary/taxonomy manager, mapping designer, diff/merge, impact preview ("what existing data breaks if I change this?"), review-and-approve workflow with roles.

SR-ONT-004.text: **Constraint validation** via SHACL-class shapes plus native rules; severity-based gates in ingestion; constraint violations visible as a graph-quality dashboard.

SR-ONT-005.text: **Business glossary and taxonomy** (SKOS-compatible): terms, synonyms, multilingual labels, definitions, owners, approved-status; terms link to ontology concepts and to physical fields; NL layer uses the glossary for grounding.

SR-ONT-006.text: **Ontology alignment/matching:** lexical, structural, embedding-assisted mapping between a customer's vocabulary and an industry standard, with confidence and steward review.

SR-ONT-007.text: **Tenant-renamable terminology (white-label semantics):** a tenant may rename "Service" → "Application", "Incident" → "Case", etc., without changing the underlying canonical type.

SR-ONT-008.text: **Ontology-driven generation:** GraphQL schema, REST resources, form UIs, validation, and docs generated from the ontology.

SR-ONT-009.text: **Governed evolution:** proposals, review, approval, scheduled rollout, backward-compat checks, automatic data migration jobs, rollback.

SR-ONT-010.text: **Catalog interoperability:** import/sync with data catalogs and glossaries (DataHub, OpenMetadata, Atlas, Collibra-class), CMDBs, enterprise-architecture repositories (ArchiMate/TOGAF models), and API registries.

SR-ONT-020.text: **Inference tiers:** (a) graph-native derivations (transitive, inverse, symmetric, property chains), (b) rule-based (Datalog/SWRL-class) materialization with provenance, (c) OWL-RL/EL profile reasoning where RDF back-ends support it, (d) probabilistic/ML inference proposals. Every inferred fact is labeled `DERIVED` or `INFERRED` and explainable ("why is this true?" returns the rule and premises).

SR-ONT-021.text: **Truth maintenance:** retraction of premises retracts conclusions; contradictions are surfaced as validation findings, never silently resolved.

SR-ONT-022.text: **Temporal and defeasible semantics** for roles/ownership that change over time (valid-time intervals on edges).

SR-RAG-001.text: **Router** chooses strategy per query class with a logged rationale; operators can override per tenant/workspace; unknown classes degrade to hybrid retrieval with a visible notice.

SR-RAG-002.text: **GraphRAG patterns:** local (entity-neighborhood + attached documents), global (community-summary map-reduce), path-based, subgraph-as-context, and temporal.

SR-RAG-003.text: **Hybrid retrieval:** BM25 + dense (+ optional sparse-learned) with reciprocal-rank fusion, cross-encoder reranking (local models), metadata/policy filtering *before* ranking.

SR-RAG-004.text: **Advanced strategies as plugins:** HyDE, query decomposition, step-back, RAG-Fusion, parent-child chunking, sentence-window, self-RAG/corrective-RAG, agentic RAG loops, long-context packing with budget manager.

SR-RAG-005.text: **Graph-aware chunking:** chunk boundaries follow document structure and link to graph entities; every chunk carries `raw_id`, section path, classification, ontology links.

SR-RAG-006.text: **Corrective verification:** before returning any LLM-generated assertion, verify entity/relationship claims against deterministic graph facts; unverifiable claims are removed or labeled.

SR-RAG-007.text: **Context budget manager:** token-aware assembly, deduplication, evidence prioritization, and per-model context-window adaptation.

SR-RAG-008.text: **Model-down fallback:** if no model is reachable, return deterministic results, retrieved evidence and templated narration with clear labeling (inherited `MVP-FR-020`).

SR-RAG-009.text: **Caching:** semantic and exact caches keyed by tenant, policy version, graph revision and model version; invalidated by revision events.

SR-RAG-010.text: **RAG evaluation harness** built in: retrieval precision/recall@k, MRR/nDCG, groundedness/faithfulness, citation precision, answer relevance, hallucination rate, latency, token cost; regression gates in CI.

SR-NLQ-001.text: **Template/semantic-parser tier first:** common intents (§1.2) compile deterministically without an LLM; an LLM-assisted tier handles open-ended phrasing using constrained decoding against the ontology schema; both emit QueryPlan IR.

SR-NLQ-002.text: **Intelligent suggestion engine (core differentiator):** when a question is ambiguous, under-specified, too broad, or maps to multiple plans, the system MUST present a ranked set of **candidate questions/queries** each with: plain-language paraphrase, the exact QueryPlan/dialect preview, expected result shape, entity bindings (with alternatives), estimated cost/latency, confidence, data-coverage note, and a permission check. The user selects and **fires** one (or edits first).

SR-NLQ-003.text: **Entity disambiguation UX:** "service account `abc`" resolving to several entities (dev/prod, duplicates across systems) shows candidates with context and lets the user pin one for the session.

SR-NLQ-004.text: **Answer modes:** (1) *Deterministic* — computed from the graph, exact, no LLM; (2) *Narrated* — deterministic facts + LLM wording; (3) *Exploratory investigation* — multi-step agent with visible plan and evidence trail; (4) *Report* — long-form, multi-section, charts/tables/citations, exportable. The UI states which mode produced the answer.

SR-NLQ-005.text: **Depth bar ("no shortness"):** answers MUST include, as relevant: direct answer, supporting evidence and paths, assumptions, confidence and uncertainty, alternatives considered, recommended next actions, coverage gaps ("sources not ingested that could change this"), and suggested follow-up questions. Minimum answer-quality gates are enforced by the evaluation suite (SR-NLQ-010).

SR-NLQ-006.text: **Explainability (XAI):** "why?" on any result returns the paths/rules/premises; counterfactuals ("what would change the answer?"); confidence decomposition (edge confidence, source freshness, coverage). Do not depend on exposing hidden model chain-of-thought.

SR-NLQ-007.text: **Conversation context:** follow-ups, pronoun/ellipsis resolution, session and saved-investigation memory, pinned entities, branching ("explore alternative"), shareable investigation links respecting each viewer's permissions.

SR-NLQ-008.text: **Reports:** templates (impact assessment, incident RCA, change-risk review, compliance evidence, executive brief), scheduled/recurring, parameterized, multi-format export (HTML, PDF, DOCX, PPTX, Markdown, JSON), evidence appendix with provenance, approval workflow, white-label styling.

SR-NLQ-009.text: **Languages:** English at P0; multilingual NL (major European, Indic and East-Asian languages) via local multilingual models at P1, with glossary-term translation.

SR-NLQ-010.text: **NL evaluation suite:** golden question sets per intent and per industry pack; metrics — intent accuracy, entity-link accuracy, plan validity rate, **execution accuracy** (result-set equality), groundedness, hallucination rate, refusal correctness, clarification precision, latency, tokens. Proposal gates: ≥ 95 % execution accuracy on Tier-1 deterministic intents; ≥ 0.95 groundedness on narrated answers; 0 policy-violating results in the adversarial set.

SR-NLQ-011.text: **Safety:** refuse or constrain questions the user is not entitled to; never reveal existence of hidden entities ("redaction notice" lists the *fact* that filters applied, not the content).

SR-NLQ-012.text: **Feedback loop:** thumbs/corrections/"this edge is wrong" feed a curation queue that improves mappings, aliases, intent templates and ranking, with steward approval.

SR-NLQ-013.text: **Voice and chat surfaces:** same pipeline via chat apps (Teams/Slack-class), IDE chat, CLI, and optional speech I/O.

SR-NLQ-014.text: **What-if simulation:** sandboxed copy-on-write overlay graph where users propose changes (delete service, rotate account, add dependency) and see propagated impact before acting; overlay never alters production truth.

SR-NLQ-015.text: **Proactive suggestions:** based on role, current entity and usage graph, the UI proposes "questions you might ask next" (e.g., owners to notify, tests to run).

SR-LLM-001.text: **Model Provider Port** for chat/completion, structured output (grammar/JSON-schema constrained), tool calling, embeddings, reranking, vision/OCR, speech; capability negotiation (context length, modalities, tools, determinism).

SR-LLM-002.text: **Local/self-hosted by default.** Adapters for local runtimes (vLLM-, SGLang-, llama.cpp-, Ollama-, TGI-, ONNX Runtime-, OpenVINO-, TensorRT-LLM-class). **No external provider adapter is active until explicitly enabled by an authorized tenant administrator** (§10.2).

SR-LLM-003.text: **Model registry:** per model — source, hash, license terms (open-weight licenses differ and some restrict commercial redistribution), intended tasks, hardware profile, evaluation scores, approval status; offline model bundles with signature verification.

SR-LLM-004.text: **Task-based routing:** small/fast models for classification, extraction and routing; larger models for synthesis; fallbacks and circuit breakers; per-tenant model allowlists.

SR-LLM-005.text: **Hardware reference configurations** (CPU-only small model; single-GPU; multi-GPU; air-gapped appliance) with sizing guidance, quantization options, throughput/latency benchmarks per release.

SR-LLM-006.text: **Prompt/skill registry:** versioned prompts, schemas, few-shot sets; A/B and regression-evaluated; tenant overrides; prompt content never contains raw sensitive data unless policy allows.

SR-LLM-007.text: **Embedding service** with model versioning, batch/online modes, multilingual and code models, and re-embedding jobs (SR-VDB-005).

SR-LLM-008.text: **LLM observability:** per-call latency, tokens, cost, cache hits, refusals, guardrail triggers, quality scores — local telemetry only unless the tenant exports it.

SR-LLM-009.text: **Guardrails:** input/output scanners (PII, secrets, injection patterns), tool allowlists, output schema validation, jailbreak/prompt-injection test corpus in CI (aligned with the OWASP LLM Top-10 categories).

SR-LLM-010.text: **Egress Gateway** is the *only* path to any external model; enforced by network policy so bypass is technically impossible.

SR-LLM-011.text: **Policy engine** evaluates every outbound call against the matrix, transforms the payload to the permitted level (schema-strip, aggregate, synthesize, tokenize, redact), and blocks on failure. Default is S0 for all tenants.

SR-LLM-012.text: **Dry-run preview:** administrators and (for S6) requesters see the *exact* payload that would be sent before approval.

SR-LLM-013.text: **Per-call Egress Manifest** (immutable): who, what data classes, which level, which fields/tokens, endpoint, region, byte counts, approval id, response hash. A "what left the building" report is exportable for auditors.

SR-LLM-014.text: **DLP and canary testing:** outbound payloads are scanned (PII/secret/PHI patterns, entropy, customer-defined dictionaries); CI plants canary values in test tenants and fails the build if any canary appears in outbound traffic below the allowed level.

SR-LLM-015.text: **Reversible tokenization vault** (local, per-tenant keys) re-identifies model responses locally; responses are also scanned before display.

SR-LLM-016.text: **Kill switch and budgets:** global/tenant/endpoint disable, rate and cost budgets, anomaly alerts on egress volume.

SR-LLM-017.text: **Consent and contract records:** enabling an endpoint records the signer, date, DPA reference, data-residency region and scope; changes require re-approval.

SR-LLM-018.text: **Same policy applies to embeddings, OCR, speech, reranking and telemetry** — not only chat models.

SR-LLM-019.text: **Local fallback:** on denial or outage, tasks fall back to local models or deterministic modes with a visible notice.

SR-LLM-020.text: **Region and sovereignty pinning:** endpoints and processing regions are constrained per tenant/jurisdiction.

SR-AGT-001.text: **Agent contract** (JSON schema): identity, purpose, allowed tools, input/output schemas, budgets (steps, tokens, time, expansions), risk class, approval mode, memory scope, evaluation hooks. Agents are data, versioned and reviewable.

SR-AGT-002.text: **Bounded runtime:** tool allowlist, budget enforcement, circuit breaker, loop/stall detection, deterministic replay from traces.

SR-AGT-003.text: **Autonomy modes:** HITL (human approves each action), HOTL (human monitors, can intervene), HIC (human in command; autonomy scoped by policy). Mode is a policy per agent × action risk class × tenant.

SR-AGT-004.text: **Read/write separation:** default agents are read-only; any write/action tool requires an explicit approval boundary, audit and (where configured) dual control.

SR-AGT-005.text: **MCP servers:** a read-only MCP server exposing graph, query, evidence and lineage tools; a separately governed action server; inventories generated from code; per-tenant auth and rate limits.

SR-AGT-006.text: **Memory:** scoped (turn/session/user/workspace/tenant), policy-governed, expiring, inspectable and erasable; no cross-tenant memory.

SR-AGT-007.text: **Agent registry & marketplace:** discover, install, evaluate and certify agents; signed packages; capability declarations.

SR-AGT-008.text: **Multi-agent orchestration:** planner/critic/worker patterns, event-driven coordination, shared evidence blackboard, XAI trace per run.

SR-AGT-009.text: **Controlled self-improvement is OFF by default;** proposals (prompt, mapping, ontology, rule changes) are generated as reviewable change requests, never self-applied.

SR-AGT-010.text: **Specialist agent catalog** (starting set inherited from the codebase, plus new): DataQuality, OntologyReview, ConnectorDiagnosis, DocumentationFreshness, EvidenceVerification, ArchitectureConformance, QueryOptimization, GraphInvestigator, KnowledgeCurator, ChangeImpact, IncidentInvestigation; new: ComplianceMapper, ImpactSimulator, ExpertFinder, KnowledgeDebt, ReportWriter, OntologyInduction, ThreatPathAnalyst.

SR-AGT-011.text: **RPA/workflow hooks:** approved agent outputs may trigger tickets, PR comments, notifications or runbook steps through connectors, always with human approval unless policy allows.

SR-AGT-020.text: **Continuous sync and change detection:** the brain updates on source change; users can **watch** an entity, pattern or question and get alerts when answers change ("continuous queries").

SR-AGT-021.text: **Drift and conformance detection:** docs vs code, architecture vs deployment, ontology vs data, policy vs access, declared vs observed dependencies.

SR-AGT-022.text: **Freshness and knowledge-decay scoring:** per node/edge/source; stale knowledge is visibly flagged and down-ranked.

SR-AGT-023.text: **Knowledge-debt and bus-factor analysis:** single-owner components, orphaned systems, undocumented critical dependencies.

SR-AGT-024.text: **Expert finder and routing:** who knows/owns/changed what, with identity-resolved evidence; "who should I ask?".

SR-AGT-025.text: **Risk scoring:** change risk = blast radius × fragility × test coverage × recent-incident correlation; surfaced in PR/change-request bots.

SR-AGT-026.text: **Anomaly detection** on graph structure, ingestion patterns and access behavior.

SR-AGT-027.text: **Digest and briefing:** scheduled personalized briefings (what changed, what's at risk, open items) per role.

SR-AGT-028.text: **Onboarding and tours:** auto-generated "map of this domain" guides for newcomers from the graph.

SR-AGT-029.text: **Digital-twin mode:** model processes/assets/organizations as simulatable graphs for scenario planning (links to SR-NLQ-014).

SR-TEN-001.text: **Tenant context is mandatory** in every API, query, job, event, cache key, log line, metric label, agent call and plugin invocation; code paths without tenant context fail closed.

SR-TEN-002.text: **Three isolation models**, selectable per tenant/edition: *Silo* (dedicated stack), *Bridge* (shared compute, dedicated data stores/namespaces), *Pool* (shared everything, logical isolation).

SR-TEN-003.text: Isolation is enforced at **every layer:** graph (database/graph-space/namespace per tenant), vector (collection), search (index), relational (schema + row-level security), object (bucket/prefix), event topics, secrets, KMS keys, caches, logs, backups, exports.

SR-TEN-004.text: **Automated cross-tenant penetration suite** (every endpoint, job type and plugin hook attempts cross-tenant reads/writes/side-channels) MUST pass in CI and before each release.

SR-TEN-005.text: **Per-tenant keys** (envelope encryption; BYOK and hold-your-own-key options), **crypto-shredding** on tenant deletion.

SR-TEN-006.text: **Noisy-neighbor control:** quotas (graph size, ingestion rate, concurrent queries, LLM tokens, storage), fair scheduling, priority lanes, per-tenant rate limits and circuit breakers.

SR-TEN-007.text: **Tenant lifecycle:** provision (API + console + IaC), configure, suspend, resume, clone (staging), migrate (cluster/region), export, delete (verified, certificate of destruction).

SR-TEN-008.text: **Per-tenant everything:** ontology extensions, connectors, mappings, model allowlist, egress policy, retention, region, SSO, branding, SLA tier, feature entitlements.

SR-TEN-009.text: **Metering and entitlements:** local, tamper-evident usage meters (records ingested, graph size, queries, LLM tokens, storage, seats, connectors) with export for billing; entitlements enforce edition/module limits; offline-capable.

SR-TEN-010.text: **Cross-tenant sharing (opt-in):** controlled sharing of ontologies, mappings, templates and anonymized benchmarks; never raw data; always explicit and auditable.

SR-WL-001.text: **Brand tokens:** logo(s), favicon, app name, colors, typography, spacing, icon sets, node/edge visual styles per ontology type, light/dark themes — all via theme packages, no code change.

SR-WL-002.text: **Domain and identity:** custom domains/CNAMEs, tenant-supplied TLS certs, branded login/SSO pages, branded transactional email, branded PDF/DOCX/PPTX/HTML reports.

SR-WL-003.text: **Terminology and persona white-labelling:** tenant renames concepts (SR-ONT-007) and names/styles the AI assistant (name, tone, avatar, greeting) without altering safety behavior.

SR-WL-004.text: **De-vendoring:** vendor identifiers removable from UI, docs, CLI binary names, container/image names, package names, API hostnames, error pages and installers; "powered by" is a licensed toggle.

SR-WL-005.text: **OEM rebuild pipeline:** partners can produce rebranded, re-signed bundles/appliance images from a documented pipeline; partner-owned update channel and docs portal.

SR-WL-006.text: **Localization packs:** UI strings, date/number formats, RTL, glossary translation; partner-supplied language packs.

SR-WL-007.text: **Custom legal and onboarding content:** terms, privacy notices, welcome tours, help links.

SR-WL-008.text: **Partner console:** create/branding/configure tenants, view fleet health and usage, apply partner policy floors, issue licenses, manage support entitlements.

SR-WL-009.text: **Embeddable components:** iframe/web-component widgets (NL console, graph viewer, impact panel) with token-based auth for embedding in customer or partner portals.

SR-CFG-001.text: **Layered configuration:** product default → edition → partner → tenant → business unit → workspace → user. Each setting is typed (JSON Schema), documented, validated, versioned and audited.

SR-CFG-002.text: **Floors and ceilings:** upper layers may set security/compliance *floors* and *ceilings* lower layers cannot loosen (e.g., tenant cannot enable external LLMs beyond partner-allowed levels). Most-restrictive-wins for security settings.

SR-CFG-003.text: **Effective-config explain:** "why does this setting have this value?" shows the layer chain and last change.

SR-CFG-004.text: **Config as code:** export/import (YAML/JSON), GitOps promotion dev → stage → prod, diff, dry-run, rollback, change approval workflow.

SR-CFG-005.text: **Feature flags and entitlements** distinct from configuration; flags never bypass policy.

SR-CFG-006.text: **Hot reload** for non-structural settings; structural changes (backend bindings, ontology major versions) go through migration plans.

SR-EXT-001.text: **Headless first:** every UI capability is available through public, versioned APIs — REST (OpenAPI 3.1), GraphQL (ontology-generated), gRPC (high-volume), WebSocket/SSE (streaming answers, subscriptions), webhooks, MCP, CLI.

SR-EXT-002.text: API standards: semantic versioning, ≥ 12-month deprecation window, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, async job pattern, consistent error model, rate-limit headers, generated reference and SDKs.

SR-EXT-003.text: **Admin APIs** cover tenants, users, config, branding, licenses, connectors, policies — enabling partner automation.

SR-EXT-004.text: Official SDKs: Python, TypeScript at P0; Java/Kotlin, Go, .NET at P1; Jupyter/notebook integrations.

SR-EXT-005.text: **Integration surface:** Slack/Teams-class ChatOps, ITSM (ServiceNow/Jira), CI/CD bots (PR impact comments, merge-risk gates), SIEM, email, calendar, BI tools (SR-ING-071), IDE extensions (VS Code at P0; JetBrains at P1).

SR-EXT-010.text: **Extension points:** connectors, parsers/extractors, relationship-discovery methods, identity-resolution matchers, graph algorithms, store adapters, query-dialect adapters, model providers, agents/skills, UI pages/widgets, report templates, validation/policy/ontology packs, notification channels, auth providers, export formats.

SR-EXT-011.text: **Isolation:** each plugin runs in a container or WASM sandbox with declared capabilities (network, filesystem, secrets, graph read/write scopes), CPU/memory/time limits, health checks and no ambient authority.

SR-EXT-012.text: **Signed, versioned packages** with manifest, compatibility range, Data-Flow Manifest, SBOM and test fixtures; trust levels (first-party / certified partner / community / private).

SR-EXT-013.text: **Plugin test kit** and scaffolding CLI; contract tests mandatory for marketplace listing.

SR-EXT-014.text: **Marketplace** (online catalog for connected profiles; **offline catalog bundles** for air-gapped): ratings, security scan results, certification badges, revenue-share support.

SR-EXT-015.text: **Low-code Studio:** visual pipeline, mapping, rule, agent and report builders that emit the same versioned artifacts as code.

SR-UX-001.text: **No mock UI:** every screen reads live APIs; hardcoded demo data is allowed only in an explicit, labeled Demo Mode. UI acceptance tests assert real backend calls.

SR-UX-002.text: **Graph visualization at scale:** WebGL rendering, level-of-detail and semantic zoom, bounded subgraph fetch, clustering/community collapse, multiple layouts (force, hierarchical, radial, geo), 2D/3D, minimap, path highlighting, blast-radius overlay; interactive at ≥ 50 k visible elements with LOD, ≥ 5 k fully detailed.

SR-UX-003.text: **Alternate views:** table, matrix (dependency/DSM), tree/hierarchy, Sankey/flow, timeline/scrubber (temporal), geo-map, diff view between revisions.

SR-UX-004.text: **Honest visual encoding:** edge style encodes class and confidence (asserted/derived/inferred/curated); freshness shading; provenance drawer ("show evidence") one click from any element or answer sentence.

SR-UX-005.text: **NL console:** suggestion cards (SR-NLQ-002), query preview (EOQL + dialect), evidence panel, mode badge (deterministic/narrated/exploratory/report), follow-up chips, investigation canvas that pins entities, paths and findings.

SR-UX-006.text: **Persona-based homes** and role-aware navigation (executive, architect, engineer, steward, auditor, admin), fully configurable.

SR-UX-007.text: **Collaboration:** comments, annotations, @mentions, shared investigations/views, review of proposed ontology/mapping changes, activity feed.

SR-UX-008.text: **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard-first, screen-reader semantics for graph (alt text paths, tabular fallback), reduced-motion, color-blind-safe palettes.

SR-UX-009.text: **Responsive and mobile read:** tablet/phone views for answers, alerts and approvals.

SR-UX-010.text: **Onboarding:** guided setup wizard (connect → profile → map → validate → ask), sample-data sandbox, in-product help, "what can I ask?" explorer driven by the meta-graph.

SR-UX-011.text: **Destructive-action safety:** confirmations with impact preview, undo where possible, dual control for configured classes.

SR-UX-012.text: **Performance budget:** initial load ≤ 3 s on reference hardware over LAN; interactions ≤ 200 ms for local operations.

SR-SEC-001.text: **Authentication:** OIDC, SAML 2.0, LDAP/AD, SCIM 2.0 provisioning, local break-glass accounts, MFA (TOTP, WebAuthn/FIDO2), scoped API keys, OAuth2 client credentials, mTLS service identities, short-lived tokens, session controls.

SR-SEC-002.text: **Authorization:** RBAC + ABAC + relationship-based (Zanzibar-style) checks + classification-based mandatory access; evaluated by a policy engine (policy-as-code, OPA/Cedar-class) with a test and **"what can this user see?" simulation** tool.

SR-SEC-003.text: **Element-level security:** policies apply to vertices, edges, properties and derived structures (embeddings, summaries, communities, caches); query-time policy rewriting and result filtering; field masking; purpose-based and time-bound (JIT) access; segregation of duties.

SR-SEC-004.text: **Permission-aware ingestion and retrieval:** where the source provides ACLs/permissions, the connector ingests and maps them so answers include only what the asking user could access in the source system; unmapped ACLs default to deny. This MUST also govern RAG context assembly and community summaries (summaries of restricted content are themselves restricted).

SR-SEC-005.text: **Access governance:** access reviews/certification campaigns, privileged-access workflows, break-glass with mandatory post-hoc review.

SR-SEC-006.text: **Agent identities** are first-class principals with least-privilege roles and budgets; agents never inherit a human's full rights implicitly.

SR-SEC-010.text: **Encryption:** TLS 1.3 externally, mTLS internally; at-rest encryption for all stores; field-level encryption for sensitive properties; KMS/HSM integration (PKCS#11, KMIP, cloud KMS adapters); rotation; optional FIPS 140-validated crypto modules.

SR-SEC-011.text: **Secrets:** mounted files/secret store only; no secrets in environment variables, images, logs, graph or embeddings; automated secret scanning on ingested content with quarantine.

SR-SEC-012.text: **Audit:** immutable, hash-chained, signed, exportable (WORM option, SIEM formats); covers authN/Z decisions, config, data access (detail configurable), policy decisions, egress manifests, admin and agent actions; retention configurable.

SR-SEC-013.text: **Hardening:** non-root containers, read-only root FS, dropped capabilities, seccomp/AppArmor profiles, minimal signed base images, network segmentation, CIS-aligned benchmarks.

SR-SEC-014.text: **Supply chain:** SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX) per image and release, VEX, signed images/artifacts (Sigstore/cosign-class), SLSA-aligned provenance, pinned and reproducible builds, license scanning, dependency review.

SR-SEC-015.text: **Secure SDLC:** threat models (STRIDE + LLM-specific + multi-tenant), SAST/DAST/SCA/fuzzing in CI, annual independent penetration test, vulnerability disclosure program, patch SLAs, security advisories channel.

SR-SEC-016.text: **Web and API defenses:** CSP, CSRF/XSS protections, SSRF guards for connectors and model endpoints, input validation, request size/time limits, DoS and abuse controls.

SR-SEC-017.text: **LLM-specific security:** prompt-injection and data-exfiltration test corpus, output filtering, tool-permission enforcement, context isolation per tenant/user (aligned with OWASP LLM Top-10 categories).

SR-PRV-001.text: **Classification engine** at ingest (patterns, dictionaries, NER, ML; customer-extensible) labels PII/PHI/PCI/secrets/IP/legal-privileged/export-controlled; labels propagate to derived data.

SR-PRV-002.text: **Data-subject requests:** locate a subject across graph, raw captures, vector/search indexes, caches, derived graphs, exports and backups (flagged); execute access/export, rectification and **erasure with propagation** (including embeddings and summaries) and produce proof.

SR-PRV-003.text: **Retention and legal hold** per class/tenant/source; automated expiry with crypto-shred option.

SR-PRV-004.text: **Purpose and consent tracking** where applicable; purpose limitation enforced in policy.

SR-PRV-005.text: **Compliance from the graph:** auto-generate records of processing, data maps, data-flow diagrams, system-to-data-class inventories, cross-border transfer views and DPIA starter reports from the graph itself.

SR-PRV-006.text: **Residency enforcement:** region pinning for storage, processing and model endpoints; cross-border transfer controls.

SR-PRV-007.text: **Pseudonymization/anonymization services** (tokenization, k-anonymity checks, optional differential-privacy aggregates).

SR-GOV-001.text: **Compliance Pack format:** control catalog, mapping to platform capabilities, automated evidence queries over the graph/audit, report templates, gap analysis.

SR-GOV-002.text: **AI governance:** model cards, AI-BOM, evaluation records, intended-use and prohibited-use settings, human-oversight configuration, user-visible AI labeling, AI incident workflow.

SR-GOV-003.text: **Change governance:** ontology, mapping, policy, model and agent changes use proposal → review → approval → rollout with audit and rollback.

SR-GOV-004.text: **Roles:** data owners, stewards, custodians, ontology curators, security admins, auditors (read-only, tamper-evident views).

SR-GOV-005.text: **Policy exceptions** are time-boxed, approved, visible and auto-expiring.

SR-NFR-001.text: **Horizontal scale** for API, query, ingestion workers, agent runners, embedding and model-serving tiers; autoscaling policies (K8s) and manual sizing for appliances.

SR-NFR-002.text: **Data scaling patterns:** graph partitioning/sharding per backend capability, read replicas, tenant-based partitioning, hot/warm/cold tiering, archive to object storage with rehydration, vector index sharding, search index lifecycle management.

SR-NFR-003.text: **Query protection:** admission control, per-tenant concurrency, cost-based throttling, kill-runaway-query, result streaming and spill, plan caching.

SR-NFR-004.text: **Graceful degradation matrix** (documented and tested): vector down → text/graph retrieval; model down → deterministic + evidence (SR-RAG-008); search down → graph-only; bus lag → stale-flag; one backend down → federated partial results with notice.

SR-NFR-005.text: **Backup/restore:** native backend backups and logical checksummed archives; consistent multi-store snapshots (graph + vector + search + relational + object + event log) with crash-atomic recovery; point-in-time recovery via event log + revisions; restore drills automated with golden-query verification.

SR-NFR-006.text: **Upgrades:** rolling and blue/green for clustered; offline signed upgrade bundles for air-gapped; versioned idempotent schema/ontology migrations; tested downgrade/rollback; compatibility matrix; LTS and stable channels (LTS ≥ 24 months).

SR-NFR-007.text: **Chaos and soak testing:** node/zone failure, partition, slow disk, clock skew, backend restart mid-ingest; 7-day soak per release.

SR-NFR-008.text: **Capacity planning tools:** sizing calculator and in-product forecasts (graph growth, index size, GPU needs) with reference architectures per tier.

SR-OPS-001.text: **OpenTelemetry** metrics, logs and traces end-to-end (ingestion → mutation → query → answer); local sinks (Prometheus/Grafana/Loki/Tempo-class) bundled; customer sinks pluggable. Structured JSON logs with correlation IDs, no secrets, no raw sensitive values.

SR-OPS-002.text: **Health and readiness** endpoints per service; dependency health roll-up; SLO dashboards and alert rules shipped as code.

SR-OPS-003.text: **Support bundle:** one command/UI action produces a redacted diagnostic archive; customer reviews before sharing.

SR-OPS-004.text: **Telemetry to vendor is OFF by default;** optional, opt-in, content-free usage statistics with a visible schema.

SR-OPS-005.text: **Runbooks** for connector failure, DLQ drain, graph restore, schema/ontology migration rollback, model outage, egress incident, tenant isolation incident, key rotation, DR failover.

SR-OPS-006.text: **Cost/FinOps views** for cloud profiles (storage, compute, LLM tokens) and capacity views for on-prem.

SR-DEP-001.text: **Docker Compose** distribution for DP-0 with healthy-start verification and one-command clean-reset demo including backup/restore (inherited `MVP-FR-028`).

SR-DEP-002.text: **Helm charts/operators** for Kubernetes (HA, autoscaling, network policies, pod security, PDBs) for DP-1…DP-4.

SR-DEP-003.text: **Offline delivery:** signed OCI image archives, model bundles, ontology/industry packs, connector catalog, docs, license file, checksum manifest; verified by an installer **preflight checker** (OS, kernel, CPU/GPU, storage, ports, time sync, certificates).

SR-DEP-004.text: **Appliance image** (hardware + software; CPU and GPU variants) with hardened OS, first-boot wizard, lifecycle updates.

SR-DEP-005.text: **Native packages** (RPM/DEB) and VM images for customers without containers.

SR-DEP-006.text: **Supported-platform matrix** (OS, kernel, Kubernetes, container runtime, browsers, GPUs) maintained and tested per release.

SR-DEP-007.text: **Offline licensing:** signed license files encoding edition, modules, size tier, tenants, seats, expiry; grace periods; **no license check may ever delete or lock customer data** (read-only degrade only); usage export for manual reporting.

SR-DEP-008.text: **Edge/federation package** for DP-6: small footprint, offline-first, delta/summary sync with conflict policies and bandwidth limits.

SR-DEP-009.text: **Reference architectures and hardening guides** per profile and tier, including network diagrams for air-gapped and connected variants.

SR-QA-001.text: Provide **synthetic dataset generators** per industry pack (referentially consistent, with planted ground-truth relationships, duplicates, drift, PII canaries and adversarial prompt-injection documents). No real customer data in test assets.

SR-QA-002.text: Each generator exposes scale knobs (S/M/L/XL) and ground-truth answers for the golden question sets.

SR-QA-010.text: Every `SR-` requirement maps to ≥ 1 executable acceptance test; the mapping is stored as structured data (test-ID → requirement-ID), **and references in comments or docstrings never count as evidence.**

SR-QA-011.text: A requirement is `Done` only if its mapped tests pass **and** a mutation/negative check proves the test fails when the behavior is broken (sampled per release).

SR-QA-012.text: Status dashboards MUST report three numbers separately: *tests passing*, *requirements with behavioral evidence*, *requirements with external-gate evidence*; a single "% complete" is prohibited.

SR-QA-013.text: Generated inventories (API routes, tools, labels, algorithms, commands) come from code introspection; hand-written counts fail the docs build.

SR-QA-014.text: Linters/type-checkers/security scanners run at zero-error policy on main (the prior baseline carried 165 lint errors, mostly mechanical).

SR-COM-001.text: **Licensing models** supported by the entitlement system: perpetual + annual support, annual subscription, size-tier/usage-based, per-tenant (OEM/managed), seat-based add-ons, revenue-share/royalty for OEM.

SR-COM-002.text: **PoC kit:** 30-day evaluation license, per-industry demo datasets, scripted demo flows, sizing tool, ROI calculator, 10-question "prove it on your data" workshop template.

SR-COM-003.text: **Legal and procurement kit:** EULA, MSA, DPA, SLA, OEM and partner agreements, BAA template, security questionnaire answers (SIG/CAIQ-style), SBOM and third-party notices, export-control classification, accessibility conformance report.

SR-COM-004.text: **Support:** Standard / Priority / Enterprise / Mission-critical tiers with response targets, escalation paths, named technical account managers, support-bundle workflow.

SR-COM-005.text: **Services:** onboarding, connector development, ontology engineering, NL tuning, training, compliance-pack onboarding, managed operations.

SR-COM-006.text: **Partner program:** certification tracks (implementer, connector developer, ontology engineer), partner portal, deal registration, co-marketing assets.

SR-COM-007.text: **Documentation set:** admin, user, API/SDK, connector developer, ontology guide, security whitepaper, architecture, reference deployments, runbooks, compliance mappings, release notes, upgrade guides, training curriculum.

SR-COM-008.text: **Sales artifacts:** datasheets per module and industry, battlecards, demo environments, reference architectures, case-study templates.

SR-COM-009.text: **Lifecycle policy:** versioning, LTS, end-of-support, security-patch commitments published.

SR-COM-010.text: **Strategy decisions to record as ADRs:** open-core vs source-available vs closed; trademark and white-label rights; third-party component redistribution rights; IP assignment for plugins and marketplace content.

SR-COM-020.text: Pack SDK and signed distribution format: ontology layer, mapping templates, connector bundles, validation/policy rules, glossary, sample dataset generator, golden questions, report templates, compliance pack references.

SR-COM-021.text: Ship the Software/IT pack and **two non-IT packs** at GA to prove horizontal applicability; remaining packs on the roadmap (§20).
